explanation: On R², a continuously differentiable field (P,Q) is conservative exactly when P_y=Q_x everywhere. For I, P_y=x²cos(xy) and Q_x=y²cos(xy), which differ, for example at (1,0). For II, both cross partials are zero, so it is conservative. For III, P_y=2y and Q_x=2x, which are not equal everywhere. Thus only II is conservative.
